title: The Tug-of-War Mystery
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about balanced and unbalanced forces.

questions.prompt: What is the net force when two equal forces act in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Equal forces in opposite directions cancel each other, so the net force is 0 N.

questions.prompt: What happens to an object when balanced forces act on it?
questions.explanation: Balanced forces do not change an object’s state of motion—velocity stays the same.

questions.prompt: In a tug-of-war, one team pulls with 70 N to the left and the other team pulls with 40 N to the right. What is the net force?
questions.explanation: Opposite forces are subtracted: 70 N − 40 N = 30 N to the left (toward the stronger pull).

questions.prompt: Which example shows balanced forces acting on a moving object?
choices: A rolling car slowing down because of friction
A cart moving at constant speed in a straight line
One tug-of-war team pulling harder than the other
questions.explanation: Constant speed in a straight line means velocity is not changing, so the forces are balanced.

questions.prompt: What can unbalanced forces do to an object's motion?
choices: Start or stop motion, change speed, or change direction
Always produce a net force of 0 N
questions.explanation: Unbalanced forces produce a nonzero net force and can start, stop, speed up, slow down, or change direction.
